items.headline: Private medical colleges bound to provide services free of cost, says Khader
items.gist: Health Minister U.T. Khader expressed strong displeasure over the lackadaisical approach of private medical colleges in providing services at government healthcare centres, saying colleges are bound to provide services free of cost.
items.paragraph: Health Minister U.T. Khader expressed strong displeasure over the lackadaisical approach of private medical colleges in providing services at government healthcare centres, saying colleges are bound to provide services free of cost. He told reporters in Mangaluru on Wednesday that if they do not abide by conditions, the State government will cancel the Memorandum of Understanding and inform the National Medical Commission. At a recent review meeting he found colleges not providing doctors and other services required under MoUs meant to fill personnel vacancies and provide specialised treatment at government hospitals; he cited Community Health Centre in Ullal as a fine example where a private institution provided four MBBS doctors, twice-a-week specialist clinics and 10 nurses, while three private medical colleges in Dakshina Kannada signed MoUs for Bantwal Taluk Hospital, Moodbidri CHC and Vitla CHC, and a private hospital is yet to start at Belthangady Taluk Hospital.

items.headline: 2 fishing boats capsize, ten people rescued
items.gist: Two wooden fishing trawlers capsized in the estuary near Mangaluru Fisheries Harbour on Tuesday evening but all 10 labourers aboard were rescued without injuries; one boat was towed ashore while the rope pulling the second snapped and it completely capsized. The vessels were Mermaid II, owned by Shareef of Alekala, Ullal, and Aniq, owned by Aboobakkar Azmal of Bengre Kasaba, Kuloor.

items.headline: Schools told to strictly adhere to safety standards for vehicles
items.gist: The Mangaluru City Traffic Police organised an awareness programme on school bus safety at Town Hall for around 600 drivers, owners and school representatives, instructing managements to adhere to Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 2012, verify vehicle and driver documents, ensure fire extinguishers and speed governors, and keep speeds below 40 kmph. DCP (Crime and Traffic) Ravi Shankar K warned that legal action would be taken against violators.

items.headline: DK administration takes steps to include missing voter's name in final electoral roll
items.gist: Admitting an error marking 63-year-old Mangaluru city resident Donald Joseph Rego as dead and removing him from the draft electoral roll, the Dakshina Kannada district administration stated steps have been taken to include his name in the final electoral roll. Additional District Electoral Registration Officer and Additional Deputy Commissioner K.
items.paragraph: Admitting an error marking 63-year-old Mangaluru city resident Donald Joseph Rego as dead and removing him from the draft electoral roll, the Dakshina Kannada district administration stated steps have been taken to include his name in the final electoral roll. Additional District Electoral Registration Officer and Additional Deputy Commissioner K. Raju said in a September 1 statement that on August 29 a BLO noticed Rego was erroneously included in the dead list and his name was deleted from the draft roll; the same day the BLO and jurisdictional ERO contacted Rego and Form 6 was submitted via the BLO App. Rego, residing on Bejai New Road and who voted in the 2024 parliament elections, found his name missing from the draft roll checked August 26 and listed as deceased in the ASDD list; after filing Form 6 on his fourth visit Wednesday, Raju said Rego had only given details in the Enumeration Form and failed to give details of himself or progeny in 2002 electoral rolls, attaching only his father's death certificate, leading the BLO to mark "No Mapping case" and during digitalisation Rego was erroneously marked dead; the ERO Mangaluru City South received the BLO explanation and the DEO served notice to the BLO.

items.headline: MCC asks unauthorised street vendors to vacate public places
items.gist: MCC asked street vendors carrying out vending without authorisation to voluntarily vacate public places, warning that if they failed to do so the corporation would evict them using Sections 12 and 18 of the Street Vendors Act, 2014. In a press release, MCC Central Zone Commissioner cited rising vehicle density and complaints that unauthorised street vendors on pavements were causing traffic obstruction and pedestrian problems.
items.paragraph: MCC asked street vendors carrying out vending without authorisation to voluntarily vacate public places, warning that if they failed to do so the corporation would evict them using Sections 12 and 18 of the Street Vendors Act, 2014. In a press release, MCC Central Zone Commissioner cited rising vehicle density and complaints that unauthorised street vendors on pavements were causing traffic obstruction and pedestrian problems. Only 667 street vendors with MCC identity cards and vending certificates are permitted; the remaining vendors were told to leave voluntarily.

items.headline: Shroom Sabha to focus on mushroom magic
items.gist: India's first mushroom festival began as a celebration of mushrooms and the mycelial networks beneath our feet, with the three-day Shroom Sabha annual nature, wellness and mushroom festival set amid the lush forests of Varanashi Organic Farms near Mangaluru. The event brings together foragers, artists, scientists, cultivators, cooks, musicians, farmers and mushroom enthusiasts through forest walks, workshops, reishi tea ceremonies, discussions on biodiversity and biomaterials, live art, music and food.
items.paragraph: India's first mushroom festival began as a celebration of mushrooms and the mycelial networks beneath our feet, with the three-day Shroom Sabha annual nature, wellness and mushroom festival set amid the lush forests of Varanashi Organic Farms near Mangaluru. The event brings together foragers, artists, scientists, cultivators, cooks, musicians, farmers and mushroom enthusiasts through forest walks, workshops, reishi tea ceremonies, discussions on biodiversity and biomaterials, live art, music and food. Organisers describe it as a movement to foster fungal literacy and reconnect people with nature, featuring sessions on healing the self, the community and the ecology.

items.headline: Road closure: Mangaluru airport-bound travellers advised to take alternate routes
items.gist: Passengers travelling from Bajpe towards Mangaluru International Airport have been advised to take alternative routes following the temporary closure of a road near Karambaru after a small bridge near the Rego Fuel Station collapsed, prompting police to shut the stretch as a safety precaution. Airport authorities have advised passengers to follow police-suggested alternative routes and leave well ahead of scheduled travel time; travellers heading towards Mangaluru and the airport should use the Jarinnagara or Porkodi roads, as should motorists travelling towards Kateel, Bajpe and Kaikamba until normal traffic movement is restored.

items.headline: I do not get works done through KRIDL, says Health Minister
items.gist: Health Minister U.T. Khader said none of the development works in his Mangaluru Assembly Constituency are executed by KRIDL, and works using rain damage grants were done by Panchayat Raj and PWD engineering wings.
items.paragraph: Health Minister U.T. Khader said none of the development works in his Mangaluru Assembly Constituency are executed by KRIDL, and works using rain damage grants were done by Panchayat Raj and PWD engineering wings. Reacting to Eshwar Khandre ordering an inquiry into Puttur MLA Ashok Kumar Rai's corruption allegations against two KRIDL engineers of Dakshina Kannada, Khader said the inquiry will bring out the truth. Shivakumar's cabinet in Mangaluru on September 18.

items.headline: Traffic between Mangaluru and Bajpe affected as minor bridge becomes unstable
items.gist: Vehicular movement between Mangaluru and Bajpe on Mangaluru-Athradi State Highway 67 was affected after an old minor bridge built in 1963 at Karambar, between MIA and Bajpe, became unstable following the collapse of a portion of its arch on Wednesday. Traffic between the city and the airport was not affected as the damaged bridge lies beyond MIA; those travelling from Bajpe to the airport and on the city–Kateel pilgrim route were disturbed, and the district administration advised road users to use Porkodi–Jokatte to reach the city and Jarinagara to reach the airport.
items.paragraph: Vehicular movement between Mangaluru and Bajpe on Mangaluru-Athradi State Highway 67 was affected after an old minor bridge built in 1963 at Karambar, between MIA and Bajpe, became unstable following the collapse of a portion of its arch on Wednesday. Traffic between the city and the airport was not affected as the damaged bridge lies beyond MIA; those travelling from Bajpe to the airport and on the city–Kateel pilgrim route were disturbed, and the district administration advised road users to use Porkodi–Jokatte to reach the city and Jarinagara to reach the airport. PWD engineers had sent reconstruction proposals years ago without government approval and will now send an emergency proposal; after temporary restoration, vehicles other than very heavy ones could ply until a new bridge is constructed.

items.headline: Elaborate security arrangements made for Vitla Pindi in Udupi
items.gist: The district police have made elaborate security and traffic arrangements for the Vitla Pindi/Krishna Janmashtami celebrations in Udupi, deploying senior officers, 186 constables, 50 Home Guards, a KSRP platoon, nine DAR platoons, fire and emergency teams, ambulances and drone teams. Seven parking locations have been identified, CCTV cameras installed at 45 additional strategic locations, and fingerprint scanners and public announcement systems arranged to manage crowds and ensure the safety of women and children.

items.headline: Three booked for scuffle near Puttur Press Club
items.gist: Puttur Town Police have registered a case against three persons and others for allegedly engaging in a scuffle and disturbing peace near the Puttur Press Club after Inspector Johnson D'Souza found several people assaulting each other despite police intervention. A case has been registered under Section 194(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita against Praveen Acharya of Mundur, Ravoof of Kurnadka and Hakeem of Bolwar, along with others.

items.headline: Boat capsizes in Gangolli estuary; fishermen flag safety concerns
items.gist: A fishing boat partially capsized in the Gangolli estuary on Wednesday but all six fishermen aboard Manjunatha Sagara were rescued by nearby purse seine boats; the vessel was later towed back to Gangolli harbour though nets and equipment were damaged. Fishermen raised concerns that a purse seine boat provided to the Coastal Security Police Station for emergencies remains non-functional a month into the fishing season.

items.headline: Three sub-inspectors suspended over bribe-for-post conversation
items.gist: Three sub-inspectors in Uttara Kannada district have been suspended after an audio recording surfaced on social media, allegedly featuring a discussion about money paid to secure the Haliyal law-and-order SI posting. In the roughly two-minute clip, the officers, who are friends, are purportedly heard discussing the alleged payment and being posted in the same taluk to make money together.

items.headline: Puttur Congress infighting surfaces after clash between workers and MLA's supporters; cops register FIR
items.gist: Internal differences within the Congress in Dakshina Kannada's Puttur came to the fore following a clash between supporters of MLA Ashok Kumar Rai and Congress workers in front of Puttur Press Club, where a heated argument allegedly turned physical in the presence of Rai. The dispute was reportedly linked to an audio clip circulating on social media; Congress worker Hakeem Koornadka had arrived to speak to mediapersons when some of the MLA's supporters allegedly confronted and surrounded him.

items.headline: All for Jawans: 8 lakh Tulasi leaves to be offered for their welfare
items.gist: A special worship featuring eight lakh Tulasi leaves will be held at the Sri Swarnavalli Mahasamsthana in Sonda on September 4 to pray for the health, safety and well-being of Indian soldiers serving along the nation's borders, as part of Sri Krishna Janmashtami celebrations. The programme will be held in the presence of Sri Gangadharendra Saraswati Mahaswamiji, Jagadguru Shankaracharya of the Sri Swarnavalli Mahasamsthana, and Sri Anandabodhendra Saraswati Mahaswamiji; special pujas will conclude with Maha Mangalarati in the afternoon followed by distribution of Teertha Prasada.
items.paragraph: A special worship featuring eight lakh Tulasi leaves will be held at the Sri Swarnavalli Mahasamsthana in Sonda on September 4 to pray for the health, safety and well-being of Indian soldiers serving along the nation's borders, as part of Sri Krishna Janmashtami celebrations. The programme will be held in the presence of Sri Gangadharendra Saraswati Mahaswamiji, Jagadguru Shankaracharya of the Sri Swarnavalli Mahasamsthana, and Sri Anandabodhendra Saraswati Mahaswamiji; special pujas will conclude with Maha Mangalarati in the afternoon followed by distribution of Teertha Prasada. The annual Tulasi worship was started during the Kargil War following a spiritual resolve by the pontiff and has entered its 27th year; devotees can collect Tulasi leaves from plants around their homes and bring them to the Swarnavalli Math on or before September 4.

items.headline: Kinnigoli-Mulki highway offers a challenge: Travel on stretch without falling into a pothole!
items.gist: The Kinnigoli-Mulki state highway has deteriorated badly, with the asphalt surface completely worn out at several stretches and potholes dotting the road, making it almost impossible for commuters to travel without falling into a pothole. The poor condition has reportedly caused several motorists, particularly two-wheeler riders, to sustain injuries; work related to the Amrut-2 drinking water pipeline further worsened the situation as the road was cut at several places and allegedly not restored properly.
items.paragraph: The Kinnigoli-Mulki state highway has deteriorated badly, with the asphalt surface completely worn out at several stretches and potholes dotting the road, making it almost impossible for commuters to travel without falling into a pothole. The poor condition has reportedly caused several motorists, particularly two-wheeler riders, to sustain injuries; work related to the Amrut-2 drinking water pipeline further worsened the situation as the road was cut at several places and allegedly not restored properly. Large potholes have developed at stretches including near S. Kodi, Sukananda Shetty Circle, the bus stand turn, Kinnigoli Rajangana, Hosakaveri Katte, Moorkaveri, Padmanuru and Kerekadu; residents said four people suffered injuries after falling from two-wheelers over the past two days, and Rs 2 crore proposed for development of the Mulki-Kinnigoli road has not yet been sanctioned.

items.headline: Six fishermen rescued
items.gist: Six fishermen were rescued from a fishing boat that capsized in the Panchagangavali estuary near Gangolli Fishing Harbour in Udupi district after the boat got stuck in the water current in the estuary and started sinking. Fishermen in the vicinity rushed and saved the six; they pulled the boat to the harbour but valuables including the fishing net were lost.

items.headline: Capt. Chowta thanks Ashwini Vaishnaw
items.gist: Dakshina Kannada MP Capt. Brijesh Chowta thanked Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Tuesday for proactive direction in bringing the Mangaluru Railway Region under South Western Railway's Mysuru division.
items.paragraph: Dakshina Kannada MP Capt. Brijesh Chowta thanked Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Tuesday for proactive direction in bringing the Mangaluru Railway Region under South Western Railway's Mysuru division. The MP met Vaishnaw in New Delhi and expressed gratitude for the August 21 Railway Ministry order excluding the Mangaluru region from Southern Railway's Palakkad division and integrating it with SWR Mysuru division, fulfilling a decades-old demand of people from Karnataka, particularly coastal Karnataka, in an administrative change bound to bring greater coherence to railway administration of the region.

items.headline: KSPC scam: CID traces money trail
items.gist: The Criminal Investigation Department, probing alleged Karnataka Public Service Commission irregularities, intensified its investigation to trace the money trail and found strong monetary leads linking the two key suspects currently in its custody, well-placed sources told DH. As many as 10 CID officers, led by a deputy superintendent of police, searched the Om Lakshmi Souharda Sahakari Sangha Niyamitha cooperative society in Lecture Colony, Bhalki in Bidar district on Wednesday; one key suspect, Basavaraj Kannale, is from Bhalki and is in CID custody along with IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, who served as Controller of Examinations at the KPSC from February 2024 to March 2026.
items.paragraph: The Criminal Investigation Department, probing alleged Karnataka Public Service Commission irregularities, intensified its investigation to trace the money trail and found strong monetary leads linking the two key suspects currently in its custody, well-placed sources told DH. Sources said an average of Rs 40 lakh was collected from each candidate and routed through this cooperative society, that Kannale had multiple accounts in relatives' names used to launder crime proceeds with Gangwar among the beneficiaries, and that among 29 candidates who allegedly paid lakhs for postings after the Veterinary Officers' Recruitment Exam is Sooguresh Jaka, said to be a relative of former KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa S Sahukar; another CID team conducted mahajars at the OMR strong room and KPSC office in Bengaluru.

items.headline: SIR: Lay greater emphasis on including names, not deleting them, Khader urges EC
items.gist: Health and Family Welfare Minister U T Khader urged officials and the Election Commission to give greater emphasis to including eligible voters rather than concentrating only on deletion during the ongoing second phase of the Special Intensive Revision, saying every citizen who has attained 18 and is eligible should be on the electoral roll. He expressed concern that people working or residing abroad could be excluded because they cannot appear in person for verification and asked the EC to explore a suitable technical or digital verification mechanism.
items.paragraph: Health and Family Welfare Minister U T Khader urged officials and the Election Commission to give greater emphasis to including eligible voters rather than concentrating only on deletion during the ongoing second phase of the Special Intensive Revision, saying every citizen who has attained 18 and is eligible should be on the electoral roll. He expressed concern that people working or residing abroad could be excluded because they cannot appear in person for verification and asked the EC to explore a suitable technical or digital verification mechanism. Khader also said food safety inspections would be intensified across Mangaluru, Hubballi, Belagavi, Mysuru and other parts of the state, announced a one-day Yuva Dasara near Thokkottu bus stand in Ullal, ordered an inquiry into KRIDL contractor harassment allegations, and said authorities were examining FSSAI rules on frozen fish sold along the coast during the fishing ban.

items.headline: Study Abroad Expo 2026 on September 6
items.gist: The Karnataka government is organising the Study Abroad Expo 2026 at Bengaluru's Palace Grounds on September 6 with around 75 global universities participating, Minister U T Khader said, describing it as a platform to help students pursue overseas education through proper channels instead of middlemen. He also announced the Karnataka State Brahmin Development Board's Sandipani Scholarship Scheme offering Rs 15,000 per year to eligible First and Second PUC and degree students, with applications open on ksbdb.karnataka.gov.in until December 31, 2026.

items.headline: NITI Aayog for 'second Bengaluru' to ease pressure on city
items.gist: Chief Minister Shivakumar said several ambitious projects are at the implementation stage to improve Bengaluru's infrastructure and appealed to NITI Aayog for special consideration for Karnataka, noting the nation's huge expectations from the state as a leader in GDP, per capita income, human development index, technology and innovation, foreign direct investment, exports, start-ups and IT services. He sought full support and requested that NITI Aayog ensure Karnataka gets its due share of Central funds, including pending grants from earlier Central Budgets.

items.headline: Nandi Hills ropeway: Panel for action on officials over violations
items.gist: A MoEF&CC expert committee deferred a decision on the Rs 93.4-crore Nandi Hills ropeway project and directed the Karnataka government to take action against officials responsible for unauthorised activities on 3.2 acres of forest land, rejecting offered compensatory afforestation lands as unsuitable and asking the state to reduce the number of trees proposed to be felled.

items.headline: Panel flags mixed waste, single-use plastic at transfer stations
items.gist: A legislature committee on local bodies inspected newly constructed garbage transfer stations in Sarvagnanagar and Shivajinagar, finding much waste mixed and single-use plastic present despite the ban, and instructed Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Ltd to create greater awareness on source segregation while planning to assess sewage treatment plants next.

items.headline: No-mapping discrepancies will be reviewed, clarifies EC
items.gist: The Bengaluru Urban district administration reviewed unnatural discrepancies in SIR digitisation in 152-Byatarayanapura constituency, finding many no-mapping cases due to missing 2002 roll details or incorrect information in parts 206, 176 and 177, and said EROs would conduct inquiries to register eligible voters in the final list without causing inconvenience.

items.headline: Juvenile held for posing as IAS officer
items.gist: A juvenile was apprehended for allegedly cheating people by creating fake Facebook accounts in the names of IAS and IPS officers to seek money, after a person was cheated through a fake account using Electronics City sub-division DCP Narayan's name and photograph. Police traced the fraud network to Kotakurd village in Rajasthan and took the juvenile into custody after serving notice to the parents on August 24.

items.headline: Tourism boost: State nod to 18 hotel projects worth ₹314.93 cr
items.gist: Karnataka has approved 18 hotel projects — eight premium and 10 budget — at the sixth Empowered Committee meeting of the Karnataka Tourism Policy, chaired by Energy and Tourism Minister K.J. George, to strengthen tourism infrastructure and attract private investment.
items.paragraph: Karnataka has approved 18 hotel projects — eight premium and 10 budget — at the sixth Empowered Committee meeting of the Karnataka Tourism Policy, chaired by Energy and Tourism Minister K.J. George, to strengthen tourism infrastructure and attract private investment. The 18 projects are expected to bring ₹314.93 crore in investment, add 655 hotel rooms and create around 1,542 jobs, with subsidies of approximately ₹47.23 crore; the committee also accorded in-principle approval to 78 additional hotel projects worth ₹1,080.97 crore, 3,424 rooms and 3,707 employment opportunities. George said improving quality accommodation was a priority and that the policy aimed to encourage private investment while strengthening local economic activity across the state.

Kumaraswamy has questioned the accountability of Minister Priyank Kharge in connection with alleged irregularities in the recruitment of RDPR engineers, even as the KPSC veterinary officer recruitment scam continues to trigger political controversy. He demanded a fair investigation into alleged irregularities involving KAS and other examinations rather than a show investigation that is later closed.

items.headline: No justice for Kargil war veteran? Land allotment delay drives him to suicide
items.gist: Retired serviceman Shivananda Reddy, who served in the Maratha Light Infantry and was injured during the Kargil War, allegedly consumed pesticide on August 28 at the Inspection Bungalow premises in Chintamani taluk, Chikkaballapura district, after a prolonged delay in allotting him land recommended in recognition of his military service. Reddy is undergoing treatment at a hospital in Bengaluru and warned in a letter that authorities would be responsible for any "untoward incidents" if his demand was not addressed.

items.headline: FIR on woman for killing 2 daughters
items.gist: An FIR has been registered against 40-year-old Uma Devi for allegedly killing her four-month-old twin daughters before attempting to take her own life at their home in Vajarahalli, Bengaluru, on Tuesday. Devi, who married Ramalingappa in 2002 and gave birth to the twins on May 5, 2026, after IVF treatment, had shown a lack of interest in the children and abnormal behaviour about one-and-a-half months after delivery and was treated for postpartum depression at Raghavendra Hospital and NIMHANS; on September 1 Ramalingappa found her attempting to hang herself with a veil and rescued her, while the twins were found dead in the same room with doctors at Shankar Hospital suspecting drowning.

items.headline: Bidar court issues injunction to stop child marriage
items.gist: An injunction has been issued by the court to prevent an individual child marriage in Bidar district, the District Child Protection Officer has stated. In connection with a child marriage scheduled to take place on Tuesday in a village in Humnabad taluk, the Judge of the Additional First Class Court, Humnabad, issued an injunction restraining the marriage under the guidance of the Deputy Commissioner and the Deputy Director, Department of Women and Child Development.

items.headline: Food safety violations will face action: Khader
items.gist: Health and Family Welfare Minister U.T. Khader has warned hotels, restaurants, catering centres and PG operators against compromising food quality, saying violators of food safety laws will face stringent action irrespective of their connections.
items.paragraph: Health and Family Welfare Minister U.T. Khader has warned hotels, restaurants, catering centres and PG operators against compromising food quality, saying violators of food safety laws will face stringent action irrespective of their connections. Addressing a media conference at the Circuit House, Khader said inspections would be expanded beyond Bengaluru to Mangaluru, Udupi, Hubballi, Belagavi and Mysuru, noting two establishments had already been shut in Bengaluru; QR and barcode stickers will be introduced to help consumers report violations. He urged PG and hostel operators to ensure hygienic, tasty and nutritious food for students, said the government was working towards NABL laboratories so adulteration test reports could withstand legal scrutiny, and ordered an inquiry into allegations raised in connection with food-related issues.

items.headline: Mysuru Dasara to witness coast's favourite Kambala for first time
items.gist: Coastal Karnataka's traditional buffalo race, Kambala, will make its official debut at the world-famous Mysuru Dasara this year, with more than 100 pairs of buffaloes from Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts expected to participate on November 18 and 19. A joint meeting of senior office-bearers of the state and district Kambala associations and buffalo owners will be held on September 10 to finalise arrangements including transportation, accommodation and veterinary support; the Dasara committee will bear transportation expenses.

A joint meeting of senior office-bearers of the state and district Kambala associations and buffalo owners will be held on September 10 to finalise arrangements including transportation, accommodation and veterinary support; the Dasara committee will bear transportation expenses. Following directions from a high-level meeting chaired by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, races will be conducted under the Tourism, Sports and Kannada and Culture departments, with the Nirmithi Kendra constructing a traditional Jodukare racing track at an estimated cost of ₹30 lakh to ₹40 lakh; a coastal food festival and cultural programmes are also planned.

items.headline: BJP's padayatra against corruption, failures of Cong govt enters day two
items.gist: Karnataka BJP's 'Ballari Chalo' padayatra to protest against alleged corruption and failures of the Congress government entered its second day on Wednesday, beginning at Santekellur in Maski and expected to cover about 22 km. items.headline: Time Out survey: Bengaluru ranks 17th among world's top destinations for nightlife
items.gist: Bengaluru ranked 17th among the world's best 20 cities for nightlife in 2026 in a Time Out survey, ahead of Accra, Singapore and Mexico City and as the only Indian city on the list. Based on responses from more than 24,000 locals worldwide on quality, affordability, diversity, safety and community feel, plus votes from city editors, culture experts and nightlife specialists, Bengaluru scored 82% for locals saying it was easy to connect with people and 71% for nightlife quality, though affordability was weaker at 54%.

items.headline: NIMHANS, prisons dept. sign MoU to strengthen inmates' mental healthcare
items.gist: The Department of Prisons and Correctional Services, Karnataka signed an MoU with NIMHANS Bengaluru for mental health support and research among incarcerated individuals. A multidisciplinary NIMHANS team will implement programmes addressing psychological and mental health concerns and strengthen the research wing of Central Prison Bengaluru, including evidence-based psychological support, psychometric assessments, psychotherapy, counselling and rehabilitative counselling.
items.paragraph: The Department of Prisons and Correctional Services, Karnataka signed an MoU with NIMHANS Bengaluru for mental health support and research among incarcerated individuals. A multidisciplinary NIMHANS team will implement programmes addressing psychological and mental health concerns and strengthen the research wing of Central Prison Bengaluru, including evidence-based psychological support, psychometric assessments, psychotherapy, counselling and rehabilitative counselling. The partnership covers workshops on psychological well-being, awareness and sensitisation on mental health, batch-wise psychosocial training on suicide prevention and substance use perils, strengthening Tele-MANAS services, and facilitating communication and visits between inmates and families.

items.headline: SC/ST quota medical seats in State see a sharp decline
items.gist: Karnataka has reverted to its earlier reservation quantum for SCs and STs in government medical seats while cases against increased reservation in recruitment are pending in the High Court. SC reserved seats fell from 953 to 906 and ST seats from 392 to 182, out of total government seats rising from 5,609 in 2025-26 to 6,045 in 2026-27; after the 2022 Act set SC at 17% and ST at 7% from 2023-24, the share reverts to 15% and 3% from 2026-27.

Community estimates suggest STs could lose about 2,800 posts and SCs about 1,400 in ongoing recruitment of roughly 72,000 vacancies, though the government says posts are kept in abeyance until a court ruling; Minister T. Raghumurthy acknowledged the decline and Devaraj T. Katur of Karnataka Rajya Nayakara Yuva Sene is fighting the reduction.

items.headline: SC terms bar council chief's tenure 'pro tem'
items.gist: The Supreme Court on Wednesday described Bar Council of India Chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra's position as only "pro tem" until a newly constituted body elects its office-bearers and directed that every policy decision of the council must involve the Attorney General and the Solicitor General. A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, hearing petitions challenging the legality of Mishra's prolonged tenure and notifications extending the terms of the chairman and vice-chairman until 2030, said it was concerned solely with the institutional functioning of the BCI and not with the conduct of any individual.
items.paragraph: The Supreme Court on Wednesday described Bar Council of India Chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra's position as only "pro tem" until a newly constituted body elects its office-bearers and directed that every policy decision of the council must involve the Attorney General and the Solicitor General. A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, hearing petitions challenging the legality of Mishra's prolonged tenure and notifications extending the terms of the chairman and vice-chairman until 2030, said it was concerned solely with the institutional functioning of the BCI and not with the conduct of any individual. Senior advocate Madhavi Divan pointed to a notification granting Mishra a five-year tenure from April 17, 2025, noting that a resolution had extended the term from three years to five years even though the BCI Rules prescribe only two years.

items.headline: IT services hiring jumps to 18-month high in September

items.headline: Non-BJP ruled states oppose 'saffronisation' of education

items.headline: Rahul’s ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event in Indore postponed, nod denied
items.gist: The Congress on Wednesday said Rahul Gandhi’s ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event in Indore, planned for September 12, has been postponed to September 19 after the Madhya Pradesh government denied permission to use Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, state Congress president Jitu Patwari announced. Patwari said the party will find a new venue, and had earlier written to Chief Minister Mohan Yadav requesting the stadium for what he described as a public dialogue on the country’s future, youth dreams, the right to education and education system security rather than a typical political event.

items.headline: Japan Credit Rating Agency lifts India a notch up on 'high growth'
items.gist: The Japan Credit Rating Agency upgraded India's credit rating one notch from BBB+ to A- on Wednesday, citing relatively high growth of around 7%, growth-oriented policies, and an improved financial system. The Finance Ministry welcomed the move, noting a higher rating would let India borrow at lower costs and reduce the exchequer's interest burden.

items.headline: Amazon India creates 1.6 lakh seasonal work
items.gist: With the festive season around the corner, Amazon India on Wednesday said it has created over 1,60,000 seasonal work opportunities across its operations network that supports e-commerce and quick commerce business. These include direct and indirect work opportunities across 400 cities in India, spanning large metros as well as tier 2 and 3 cities like Varanasi, Kochi, Jalandhar, Ghaziabad, Ranchi, Salem and Gorakhpur.

items.headline: 7.8% or 2.6% GROWTH FIGURES REAL OR BOGUS?
items.gist: Former RBI Governor Raghuram Rajan has questioned whether India's 7.8 per cent GDP growth for Q1 FY27 adequately reflects ground realities, a day after MoSPI reported the figure, significantly above the RBI's 7 per cent estimate. Former Finance Secretary Subhash Chandra Garg argued growth would have been around 2.6 per cent if the previous year's GDP had not been revised down from around ₹86 lakh crore to ₹80 lakh crore—a calculation Statistics Secretary Saurabh Garg rejected as an "apples and oranges" exercise mixing two different GDP series.

items.headline: Maha BJP accuses Congress of opposing women's reservation
items.gist: BJP leaders protested in Nashik on Wednesday against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi's visit, accusing his party of opposing women's representation in Parliament and state assemblies. Nashik BJP MLA Devayani Farande and Mayor Himgauri Aher-Adake led a protest march in black sarees with "Go back" slogans, citing the defeat in April of a Constitution Amendment Bill intended to provide 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies from 2029.

items.headline: Andhra literacy rate up to 82% from 72% in 2 years: Minister
items.gist: Andhra Pradesh Education Minister Nara Lokesh said on Wednesday that the state's literacy rate rose from 72.6 per cent in 2024 to 82.1 per cent in 2026, describing it as a "truly historic" transformation under the Akshara Andhra mission launched by the NDA government in 2025. Lokesh said Andhra Pradesh had one of the lowest literacy rates when he took charge in 2024, below even Bihar at 74.3 per cent, but moved above the national average of 81 per cent in two years, with around 25 lakh people becoming literate through the initiative.

Lokesh said Andhra Pradesh had one of the lowest literacy rates when he took charge in 2024, below even Bihar at 74.3 per cent, but moved above the national average of 81 per cent in two years, with around 25 lakh people becoming literate through the initiative. He directed officials to work in mission mode to achieve 100 per cent literacy by September 2027 and prepared a phased plan to make another 25 lakh people literate by March 2027.

items.gist: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu directed TTD and Endowments Department officials to expedite construction of 5,000 temples across the state and finalise sites at the earliest, an official release said late on Tuesday. items.headline: 787 riders fined Rs 7.87 lakh over helmet
items.gist: Police in Maharashtra's Latur district launched a helmet enforcement drive on Tuesday, booking 787 two-wheeler riders for riding without protective headgear and collecting Rs 7.87 lakh in fines on the first day. Officials said awareness campaigns on helmet use had been conducted since March, but compliance remained below expectations, prompting strict enforcement from September 1, and added that the drive was not aimed at collecting fines.

items.headline: DC urges Jarange to end fast as doctors flag health concerns on day five of protest
items.gist: Activist Manoj Jarange's hunger strike over the Maratha reservation issue entered its fifth day on Wednesday in Jalna district, as doctors raised concerns over his deteriorating health and Jalna district collector Ashima Mittal appealed to him to end his fast. A medical officer said Jarange's blood sugar level had dropped, and doctors camping at the protest site urged him to take IV fluids, which he refused.
items.paragraph: Activist Manoj Jarange's hunger strike over the Maratha reservation issue entered its fifth day on Wednesday in Jalna district, as doctors raised concerns over his deteriorating health and Jalna district collector Ashima Mittal appealed to him to end his fast. A medical officer said Jarange's blood sugar level had dropped, and doctors camping at the protest site urged him to take IV fluids, which he refused. Jarange began his indefinite hunger strike at Antarwali Sarati on August 29, demanding reservation for Marathas and immediate issuance of Kunbi certificates on the basis of gazette records, and has threatened to intensify the agitation and take it to Mumbai if demands are not met. Mittal met Jarange on Tuesday night to explain government steps on Maratha reservation, but he questioned whether she had come to defend the government's position.

items.headline: CM Naidu releases Godavari water to North Andhra
items.gist: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday released Godavari waters to North Andhra through the Polavaram Project Left Main Canal, marking a major step towards strengthening irrigation and drinking water supply in the region. The Chief Minister performed 'Jala Harathi' at Payakaraopeta in Anakapalli district and switched on the regulator, allowing water to flow through canals, rivers, aqueducts and syphons via the Pampa, Tandava, Varaha and Sarada rivers and the Yeleru canal.
items.paragraph: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday released Godavari waters to North Andhra through the Polavaram Project Left Main Canal, marking a major step towards strengthening irrigation and drinking water supply in the region. The Chief Minister performed 'Jala Harathi' at Payakaraopeta in Anakapalli district and switched on the regulator, allowing water to flow through canals, rivers, aqueducts and syphons via the Pampa, Tandava, Varaha and Sarada rivers and the Yeleru canal. The Rs 4,192-crore canal, constructed over 213 km, will initially provide irrigation to 2.87 lakh acres in four districts and drinking water to around 5.23 lakh people, with specialised structures including a 447-metre aqueduct across the Tandava river designed to carry up to 10,634 cusecs of water.

items.headline: 'Handing hostels to RSS-linked trust'
items.gist: A tribal rights group has launched an agitation in Nagpur, alleging that the Maharashtra government has handed over the operations of nearly 500 tribal hostels to an "RSS-linked" trust, a claim officials rejected as "baseless." The Adivasi Adhikar Bachhav Kriti Samiti, which started its protest on Monday, said it would stage a peaceful demonstration at the RSS headquarters in Nagpur if the government did not revoke the decision. Co-coordinator Rajat Maheshgawli claimed the government has "fully handed over" 490 tribal hostels to the Late Laxmanrao Mankar Memorial Trust under an MoU with the Tribal Development Department, calling it a conspiracy to privatise tribal hostels and saying arrangements for tribal students' education, nutrition, accommodation, safety and basic rights must be free from interference.

items.headline: Hyderabad SIR deletions exceed 2023 winning margins in all 15 constituencies, finds report
items.gist: Deletions in draft electoral rolls across 15 Hyderabad Assembly constituencies under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exceed the 2023 winning margin in every constituency, according to an analysis by Kolkata-based Sabar Institute. Muslim electors account for 40.7% of the 19,41,444 deletions in Hyderabad, ranging from 12.1% in Secunderabad Cantonment to 85.9% in Bahadurpura; in Malakpet and Yakutpura deletions exceed total votes polled in 2023.

Statewide, 73.39 lakh voters were deleted from Telangana’s 17 August draft roll—21.3% of the electorate—with ECI officials noting the exercise is ongoing and comparing 2023 absolute voter numbers with ASDD figures frozen on 12 May.

items.headline: NESt Fest to showcase Northeast’s culture, youth talent in Delhi on September 4-5
items.gist: The ninth edition of the North East Students’ Festival (NESt Fest) will be held in New Delhi on September 4 and 5, showcasing the region’s culture, student talent, music, handicrafts, cuisine and youth voices. items.headline: Death toll 14: House of UP’s cracker factory blast accused razed
items.gist: Authorities have razed a three-storey house of main accused Naushad in the illegal cracker factory blast in Manouri town, Kaushambi, as the death toll rose to 14 after Urvashi (17) succumbed to injuries at SRN hospital in Prayagraj on Wednesday. Police raided a warehouse owned by his wife Kahkashan Bano, seized six sacks of firecrackers, demolished Naushad’s unauthorised house in an 11-hour operation, arrested Naushad along with Shabana and Saina, and are hunting three others with Rs 25,000 rewards each while collecting evidence to invoke the NSA; nine police personnel were suspended for alleged negligence after the August 31 blast killed 11 children and damaged houses within about 100 metres, with three properties collapsing completely.

items.headline: Mettur dam cost Rs 4.8 cr, but Vijay’s visit cost Rs 5 cr: TN BJP chief
items.gist: BJP leader Nainar Nagenthran claimed on Wednesday that the Tamil Nadu administration spent Rs 5 crore on Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s recent visit to Mettur Dam, alleging the travel expenditure exceeded the Rs 4.80 crore historical cost of constructing the reservoir itself. Terming Vijay a “costly Chief Minister,” Nagendran questioned deploying barricades and spending public funds when the dam held only partial capacity, and accused the state government of failing delta farmers as Mettur’s sluice gates, traditionally opened on June 12, faced delays due to acute water shortage.

items.headline: LDF in turmoil, strong dissent against CPI(M) leadership: Keralam CM Satheesan
items.gist: Keralam Chief Minister V D Satheesan said on Wednesday that the ruling LDF was in “turmoil,” with CPI(M) and CPI locked in a bitter war of words and strong dissent brewing against CPI(M) leadership, while the Congress was “watching it from outside and enjoying it.” Responding to the Left allies’ row over the Deputy Leader of Opposition post, he accused the CPI(M) of mobilising its student and youth wings for violent street protests to divert attention from party issues, apparently referring to Tuesday’s SFI march over the complete rendition of Vande Mataram at an event attended by Vice President C P Radhakrishnan, during which several activists were injured in a clash with police.

items.headline: Withdrawal of cases standard admin practice: DMK on Vijay
items.gist: Senior DMK leader T K S Elangovan on Wednesday downplayed the political significance of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s decision to withdraw police cases against protesting farmers and teachers, calling it standard administrative practice and noting previous DMK governments had done the same when people fought for their rights. Vijay told the Assembly that cases against farmers who peacefully protested Parandur airport and SIPCOT expansion, and against teachers who protested democratically, would be dropped; Elangovan also dismissed speculation about TMC MP Saayoni Ghosh joining Vijay’s party and rejected suggestions Vijay could be a 2029 prime ministerial face, saying his TVK government lacks an absolute majority in Tamil Nadu.

items.headline: SIR is helping BJP, SC must stop deletions: Sibal
items.gist: Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal on Wednesday alleged that the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is aimed at helping the BJP win elections and urged the Supreme Court to stop “bulk deletions,” citing an Indian Express report that BJP agents in Godda, Jharkhand, sought to delete voters mostly from the minority community. At a press conference, Sibal said BJP workers were filing bulk Form 7 deletion requests without giving reasons and that targeted names belonged to the Muslim community, with affected residents saying their families had lived there for years.

items.headline: Keralam lays groundwork for India’s first electric truck corridor on NH 66
items.gist: Keralam is preparing to develop the 622-km National Highway 66 stretch from Kasaragod to Thiruvananthapuram as India’s first electric truck corridor, with a KSEBL–ICCT study finding an initial 12.5 MW charging network requiring Rs 19 crore investment and projecting 1,939 chargers with 204.5 MW combined capacity and Rs 338 crore investment by 2050. Researchers used FASTag, GPS and parking data from 13,355 trucks along the corridor; Kochi, Kozhikode and Kollam are expected to emerge as major charging hubs, and KSEB said the project can draw from central PM E-DRIVE scheme funds and Rs 63.12 crore already sanctioned for Keralam’s charging network.

items.headline: JioHotstar launches services in UK, Canada, Singapore
items.gist: JioHotstar, the OTT platform owned by JioStar, on Wednesday announced its international launch in the UK, Canada and Singapore, marking its foray into becoming a global entertainment platform with over 1,60,000 hours of content across 12-plus languages. items.headline: Gen Z missing career opportunities due to fear of being judged: Report
items.gist: Fear of being judged holds back the majority of Gen Z professionals from connecting or networking with people who could help them in their careers, a LinkedIn report said on Wednesday, with 83 per cent of India's Gen Z professionals hesitating to interact or network with such people. Fear of being judged (44 per cent), concerns about bothering others (39 per cent) and worries about sounding inauthentic (37 per cent) are preventing Gen Z from seeking valuable advice and making connections, according to a Censuswide survey of 18,050 respondents conducted between July 20 and August 11, 2026 across countries including India.

items.headline: Strictly follow food safety norms: FSSAI tells 5-star hotels
items.gist: Food Safety Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) CEO Rajit Punhani, in a meeting with senior executives of major hotel companies held on Tuesday, asked all leading 5-star hospitality firms in the country to strictly follow food safety norms and ensure hygiene benchmarks, asserting zero tolerance for any violations. The direction comes in the wake of FSSAI's recent notices to two major 5-star hotels, JW Marriott and Andaz at Aerocity in Delhi, and amid an enhanced drive and stringent actions against food safety violations.

items.headline: Modi govt defends new GDP estimates
items.gist: The statistics ministry on Wednesday defended the methodology behind its newly released economic growth estimates, saying revisions to last year's GDP and the divergence between different price measures reflect updated data and estimation techniques rather than an attempt to artificially boost headline growth. India's economy grew 7.8 per cent in real terms in the first quarter of fiscal 2026-27 according to the revised GDP series, which uses 2022-23 as the base year and incorporates a new Producer Price Index, Banking Services Price Index and additional administrative data.
items.paragraph: The statistics ministry on Wednesday defended the methodology behind its newly released economic growth estimates, saying revisions to last year's GDP and the divergence between different price measures reflect updated data and estimation techniques rather than an attempt to artificially boost headline growth. India's economy grew 7.8 per cent in real terms in the first quarter of fiscal 2026-27 according to the revised GDP series, which uses 2022-23 as the base year and incorporates a new Producer Price Index, Banking Services Price Index and additional administrative data. The ministry rejected claims that the Q1 2025-26 current-price GDP estimate was reduced from Rs 86.05 lakh crore to Rs 80 lakh crore to make the latest growth rate appear stronger, noting the Rs 86.05 lakh crore figure was under the superseded 2011-12 base-year series and was revised to Rs 80.32 lakh crore when the 2022-23 base-year series was introduced in February 2026.

items.headline: 'Share of electricity in India's energy mix to reach 45-50%'
items.gist: India will double the share of electricity in its total energy mix to 45-50 per cent by 2047 from 22 per cent at present, Central Electricity Authority Chairperson Ghanshyam Prasad said on Wednesday at Bharat Electricity 2026, POWERGEN India & Indian Utility Week 2026. Last year India added a record 64,000 MW of new capacity, with more than 50,000 MW from renewables alone, and this year is likely to surpass that with up to 70,000 MW of fresh additions; by 2035 India is poised to double its 2030 renewables target, reach 100 GW of pumped hydro storage by 2035-36 and achieve 100 GW of nuclear power by 2047.

Last year India added a record 64,000 MW of new capacity, with more than 50,000 MW from renewables alone, and this year is likely to surpass that with up to 70,000 MW of fresh additions; by 2035 India is poised to double its 2030 renewables target, reach 100 GW of pumped hydro storage by 2035-36 and achieve 100 GW of nuclear power by 2047. Prasad said Rs 4 lakh crore (USD 40 billion) in transmission projects are underway to evacuate 266 GW, with 600 GVA of transformation capacity planned to provide grid connectivity for new renewables within 24-36 months.

items.headline: India's e-commerce market to hit $ 345 bn by 2030; dark stores to triple, says a report
items.gist: India's e-commerce sector is projected to grow nearly three times to USD 345 billion by 2030 from USD 125 billion in 2024 at a compound annual growth rate of 18.4 per cent through 2030, according to a report titled 'Smart Growth in a Fast Market' by research consultancy Infisum released on Wednesday. The country's dark store network is set to nearly triple from 2,525 in 2025 to approximately 7,500 by 2030, with quick commerce valued at an estimated USD 65-70 billion by 2030 and expected to contribute 45-50 per cent of incremental e-retail growth; Blinkit leads with a 44 per cent market share, followed by Zepto and Swiggy Instamart at 25 per cent and 20 per cent respectively.

The country's dark store network is set to nearly triple from 2,525 in 2025 to approximately 7,500 by 2030, with quick commerce valued at an estimated USD 65-70 billion by 2030 and expected to contribute 45-50 per cent of incremental e-retail growth; Blinkit leads with a 44 per cent market share, followed by Zepto and Swiggy Instamart at 25 per cent and 20 per cent respectively. By the end of the decade e-commerce is expected to account for 10-12 per cent of India's total retail spending and contribute 2.5 per cent to the national GDP, serving an estimated 420-440 million online shoppers.

items.headline: Flexi-cap funds attract nearly Rs 50,000 cr
items.gist: Flexi-cap mutual fund schemes attracted nearly Rs 50,000 crore in net inflows during January-July 2026, marking a 27 per cent increase over the year-ago period, as investors increasingly favoured equity strategies that can dynamically move across market-cap segments. Flexi-cap fund folios rose to 2.44 crore in July 2026 from 1.94 crore a year earlier, adding around 50 lakh investor accounts, while assets under management of the category stood at around Rs 6 lakh crore as of July 2026, up from Rs 4.94 lakh crore in July 2025, according to data from the Association of Mutual Funds in India (Amfi).

items.headline: L&T Finance plans to add 500 gold loan branches

items.headline: In insolvency case, Chandra opposes NCLT
items.gist: Essel Group Chairman Subhash Chandra on Wednesday opposed the formation of a five-member bench by the NCLT to decide his personal insolvency case, contending that the tribunal does not have the power to constitute such a bench, with Senior Advocate Sasmit Patra appearing for him before the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) terming the NCLT order faulty and wrong. The five-member bench had on Tuesday stayed the order of Nilesh Sharma, Member (Judicial), who was brought in as the third member after a division bench of the NCLT delivered a split verdict; NCLT on Tuesday barred Chandra from alienating his assets and stayed an order allowing him to settle claims arising from personal guarantees on group borrowings for about Rs 6.5 crore against claims of roughly Rs 22,006 crore.

items.headline: Formulate rules for fishing vessel transit to EEZ, SC directs T.N.
items.gist: The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed Tamil Nadu to frame rules creating a "specified channel" or official navigation corridor under the Marine Fishing Regulation Rules 2020 for transit of vessels from territorial waters to the EEZ for purse seine fishing. A Division Bench of Justices P.S.
items.paragraph: The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed Tamil Nadu to frame rules creating a "specified channel" or official navigation corridor under the Marine Fishing Regulation Rules 2020 for transit of vessels from territorial waters to the EEZ for purse seine fishing. A Division Bench of Justices P.S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe upheld both the state's Marine Fishing Regulation Rules 2020 and the Centre's Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the EEZ Rules 2025, noting the EEZ Rules contemplate an "access pass," after the state raised concern that fishers could employ purse seine nets within territorial waters under the guise of EEZ fishing. The court held that rights and liabilities are governed by the relevant laws and said there is no conflict between the Union's EEZ Rules and Tamil Nadu's marine fishery regulation rules.

items.headline: SC seeks govt. explanation on IPS deputation in CAPFs
items.gist: The Supreme Court on Wednesday sought an explanation from Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan on implementing its May 23, 2025 judgment to progressively reduce IPS deputation to senior CAPF posts within two years, as Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said cadre officers were "completely stifled". An affidavit said 46 IPS officers were brought on deputation to CAPFs up to the SAG level after the judgment, while the government enacted the CAPFs (General Administration) Act, 2026, published on April 9, now challenged in five writ petitions listed for November 18.

items.headline: Bhupathi: from dreaded Maoist to Gondwana University coordinator
items.gist: Bhupathi, once a Maoist with a ₹6 crore bounty wanted in six States, surrendered with 60 others on October 15, 2025, before Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, and has now been selected coordinator at Gondwana University's Village Council Capacity Building and Training Centre. Coordinators will visit Gadchiroli villages to supervise Gram Sabhas and create awareness of tribal rights under PESA, receiving a ₹30,000 monthly stipend and travel allowance.

items.headline: What's the reason behind the sudden surge in onion prices?
items.gist: On September 1, the all-India average onion price was ₹49.59 a kg, up over 74% from ₹28.48 on the corresponding day in 2025, though production is estimated at 307.37 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, in line with last year's 307.67 lakh tonnes. Industry sources cite lower-quality harvests after delayed rains in Maharashtra, hoarding by big traders, and seasonal festive demand; the government has begun calibrated buffer releases, selling onions at ₹35 a kg.

items.headline: Can jurists be appointed as Supreme Court judges?
items.gist: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan questioned at NLU Delhi's 13th LL.M. convocation why Article 124(3)'s route for appointing a 'distinguished jurist' as a Supreme Court judge has remained unused for more than 76 years, noting no legal academic has been elevated under the provision while judges have overwhelmingly come from High Court benches and only 11 advocates were directly elevated from the Bar.
items.paragraph: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan questioned at NLU Delhi's 13th LL.M. convocation why Article 124(3)'s route for appointing a 'distinguished jurist' as a Supreme Court judge has remained unused for more than 76 years, noting no legal academic has been elevated under the provision while judges have overwhelmingly come from High Court benches and only 11 advocates were directly elevated from the Bar. The explainer traces Constituent Assembly intent to diversify the Bench, the rejected and later omitted High Court jurist provision, and barriers including Collegium recommendation and restrictions on full-time law teachers practising as advocates.

items.headline: Nepal flash flood death toll rises to 1,127
items.gist: The death toll from Nepal's devastating flash floods rose to 1,127 on Wednesday as rescuers raced to find thousands still missing a week after the Himalayan disaster, police said. Nepal Police recovered 348 bodies from Chitwan, 217 from Nawalparasi East, 190 from Nawalparasi West, 155 from Nuwakot and others from Gorkha, Dhading, Rasuwa and Tanahu; postmortem and legal identification procedures had been completed for 1,113 bodies and 95 had been handed over to relatives.
items.paragraph: The death toll from Nepal's devastating flash floods rose to 1,127 on Wednesday as rescuers raced to find thousands still missing a week after the Himalayan disaster, police said. Security forces have rescued 6,541 people from affected areas while search operations continued, and details of 911 unidentified bodies were uploaded to the Nepal Police website to help families identify relatives.

items.headline: US-Iran strikes deepen Middle East crisis
items.gist: The United States military struck targets in Iran on Tuesday as hostilities flared after a month without military action, and Iran fired missiles and drones in response, according to Iranian semiofficial media Fars and Tasnim. One US strike hit a home hosting a wedding, killing five people and wounding dozens, local officials said, while US Central Command said the strikes followed Tehran's attempts to attack commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and US service members in the region.

items.headline: FBI seizes $5,60,000 in Hamas crypto funds
items.gist: The FBI has seized more than USD 560,000 in cryptocurrency donations intended for Hamas, the Justice Department said Tuesday. In addition to seizing cryptocurrency meant to support Hamas' military wing, the department took control of website domains and communication platforms used for fundraising and recruitment, and obtained information about thousands of people who had contacted Hamas with a goal of giving money to the group.

items.headline: When roads end, drones carry dead in Nepal
items.gist: In flood-ravaged hills of Nepal, drones airlifted seven bodies this week from Devighat-3 in Nuwakot to Devighat-5 from an area so difficult and dangerous that rescuers could not safely reach it. The operation involved personnel from Nepal Police, Nepal Army and drone manufacturer GarudX, and reflects how drones are quietly becoming an extra pair of hands in Nepal's disaster response—ferrying food and medicines to cut-off communities, searching inaccessible areas and airlifting bodies from locations too dangerous for rescuers.

items.headline: Xi visits Egypt as China seeks Mideast influence
items.gist: Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to Egypt this week strengthens economic and diplomatic ties as China, the United States' top global rival, cultivates an extensive relationship with one of America's key Middle East allies amid efforts to expand its influence in the rapidly changing region. Xi aims to present China as a stabilizer in the region and contrast it with the United States, whose six-month war with Iran is the latest example of decades of military entanglement there.

items.headline: Levels in 3 Nepal rivers cross danger mark
items.gist: Nepalese authorities on Wednesday urged people living in the central, western and eastern parts of the Himalayan nation to remain alert after water levels in three major rivers crossed alert levels following rainfall in different parts of the country. According to the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology's Flood Forecasting Division, the Sun Koshi River in Sindhuli district, the Budhi Gandaki River in Gorkha and the Mahakali River were above alert levels, and the Marsyangdi River in Lamjung crossed the danger mark at the Bhukundebesi water level monitoring centre at 11:15 PM Tuesday with levels still on the rise.

items.headline: Earth is heating past the safe limit; now, the UN wants a way back
items.gist: In a strategic retreat in the fight against climate change, the United Nations has acknowledged that Earth has lost its chance to prevent some of global warming's worst harms and must now figure out how to get temperatures below the danger zone and back to safety. Earth is soon going to exceed the safe temperature threshold agreed upon in the 2015 Paris climate accord because of warming from the burning of coal, oil and gas, according to a bleak first-of-its-kind report issued Wednesday by the United Nations Environment Programme.
items.paragraph: In a strategic retreat in the fight against climate change, the United Nations has acknowledged that Earth has lost its chance to prevent some of global warming's worst harms and must now figure out how to get temperatures below the danger zone and back to safety. Earth is soon going to exceed the safe temperature threshold agreed upon in the 2015 Paris climate accord because of warming from the burning of coal, oil and gas, according to a bleak first-of-its-kind report issued Wednesday by the United Nations Environment Programme. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said humanity is speeding past the limit to avoid climate catastrophe, and the new strategy envisions getting back below the threshold by ending fossil fuel use and developing ways to remove industries' carbon dioxide from the air.

items.headline: UN charts course to manage global warming-limit breach
items.gist: Warning that a breach of the 1.5 degrees Celsius global warming limit will bring irreversible ecological losses, the United Nations Environment Programme on Wednesday set out a detailed "overshoot, peak, and decline" pathway for the first time. The Limiting Overshoot report said global warming would cross 1.5 degrees Celsius in the next few years; even if every country delivers on its national climate plan and net-zero target, peak warming would reach 1.8 degrees Celsius, while current policies point to a rise of about 2.6 degrees Celsius by 2100.

items.headline: An alternative emerges to check Japan's bear troubles
items.gist: As rising bear attacks bring fear across Japan — six people killed nationwide since April 1 after a record 13 fatal attacks last fiscal year, and a record 14,000 bears culled last fiscal year — Nagano's pioneering coexistence programme since 1995 offers an alternative to mass culling through trapping, tagging, and releasing bears, Karelian Bear Dogs, and more than 3,000 km of fencing. Scientist Akiko Takii argues the approach has helped form a healthy bear population and limit dangerous encounters, with annual sightings broadly stable at around 1,400 in recent years, compared with 59 encounters and four deaths in Akita and five fatalities in Iwate last year.

items.headline: Tilak guides South Zone to Duleep Trophy final
items.gist: Skipper Tilak Varma played a second successive influential knock, guiding South Zone to the Duleep Trophy final with a seven-wicket win over North Zone on the fourth and final day of the semifinal in Bengaluru on Wednesday. Chasing 181, South Zone finished 182 for three as Tilak remained unbeaten on 51 and Ravichandran Smaran was 32 not out in an unbroken 80-run fourth-wicket stand, and South will face East Zone in the title clash in Chennai from September 6 after Tilak's unbeaten 116 in the first innings had helped secure a 117-run lead.

items.headline: Asia Cup: India must fix batting frailties against Hong Kong
items.gist: India will need to sort out batting frailties for a more complete performance when they face Hong Kong in their second match of the Women's T20 Asia Cup in Dubai on Thursday. After sitting at 101 for two after 10 overs in their opening win over Thailand, India lost seven wickets for 29 runs to finish at 159 for nine before winning by 94 runs; Shafali Verma scored 64 and Deepti Sharma took three wickets without conceding a run, but Smriti Mandhana, Pratika Rawal and skipper Harmanpreet Kaur will want better returns ahead of bigger battles including against Pakistan and the Asian Games in Japan.

items.headline: Gambhir, Agarkar to review injury list, World Cup plans
items.gist: Head coach Gautam Gambhir and selection committee chairman Ajit Agarkar will meet BCCI officials in New Delhi on Thursday to discuss injury management for key players ahead of the October–November New Zealand tour and the roadmap for next year's ODI World Cup. The June–July UK debacle is expected to be reviewed, but stakeholders including secretary Devajit Saikia want to look ahead, with COE head VVS Laxman also expected to attend; Agarkar and Gambhir are seeking clarity on centrally contracted injured players such as Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya at the Bengaluru COE, and on fitness timelines for Bumrah, Washington Sundar, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Harshit Rana named subject to fitness for the Afghanistan T20I series from September 13.

items.headline: US Open: Zverev outlasts Sonego in wild five-setter to reach second round
items.gist: Top-seeded Alexander Zverev scraped into the US Open second round on Tuesday, beating 89th-ranked Lorenzo Sonego 6-4, 3-6, 6-7 (7/9), 7-5, 6-4 on Arthur Ashe Stadium after four hours and 53 minutes, finishing at 1:55 a.m. Zverev said it was nearly five hours for a first-round match and the longest first-round match he had ever played, notching his seventh win in seven meetings against Sonego and booking a second-round meeting with France's Quentin Halys while avoiding becoming the first men's top seed in 23 years to fall in a Grand Slam first round.

items.headline: Gill, Bumrah slip; Padikkal moves up in Test rankings
items.gist: Captain Shubman Gill slipped two positions to ninth among batters and Jasprit Bumrah dropped one spot among bowlers in the latest ICC Test rankings released on Wednesday, while Devdutt Padikkal rose five places to 54th among Indians. Gill returned with only one half-century across three innings on the Sri Lanka tour, wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant remains the highest-ranked Indian batter at seventh, Yashasvi Jaiswal is unchanged at 11th, and Padikkal moved up after scoring 328 runs across two Tests with two centuries on the tour.

items.headline: Selector Auqib Javed wants inquiry into Imam's injury, defends recalling 7 players
items.gist: Pakistan Cricket Board selection committee member Aaqib Javed has questioned the severity of Imam-ul-Haq's calf injury and called for an inquiry into treatment protocols after the opener did not bat during Pakistan's 194-run loss to England in the second Test at Lord's last Sunday. Javed told Geo TV that an inquiry will be conducted, asking how Imam failed to come out to bat in both innings after pulling a muscle, and said action will be taken while defending the panel's decision to recall seven players.

items.headline: 'Playing Brazil, Uruguay will be turning point for Indian football'
items.gist: India head coach Khalid Jamil said playing five-time world champions Brazil and two-time winners Uruguay at home is a dream come true and will prove a turning point in the history of Indian football while helping prepare for next year's Asia Cup qualifiers. Jamil told PTI that India is playing Brazil for the first time in history, the main target is 2027 Asia Cup qualification, and that with full fan support the players will be motivated to perform well against top teams that will help them gain confidence through more matches.

items.headline: The endurance blueprint: Mastering hydration for workouts and long runs
items.gist: Hydration is often called the “fourth macronutrient” of athletic endurance, and fluid management directly dictates endurance capacity, cardiovascular output, and recovery speed—losing as little as 2% of body weight in fluids impairs aerobic performance, elevates heart rate, and increases perceived exertion, while thirst is a delayed indicator of loss. The piece explains how dehydration affects cardiovascular efficiency, thermoregulation, and nutrient delivery; warning signs from mild dehydration (1–3% body weight loss) through heat exhaustion and heat stroke; how to calculate personal sweat rate via a sweat test; and a three-phase strategy covering pre-hydration (24 hours to 30 minutes before), during-workout replacement every 15–20 minutes (16–28 oz per hour), and post-run recovery at 125–150% of weight lost over 2–4 hours.

The piece explains how dehydration affects cardiovascular efficiency, thermoregulation, and nutrient delivery; warning signs from mild dehydration (1–3% body weight loss) through heat exhaustion and heat stroke; how to calculate personal sweat rate via a sweat test; and a three-phase strategy covering pre-hydration (24 hours to 30 minutes before), during-workout replacement every 15–20 minutes (16–28 oz per hour), and post-run recovery at 125–150% of weight lost over 2–4 hours. It also contrasts plain water with electrolyte replacement, noting sweat carries roughly 200–1,500 mg of sodium per liter alongside potassium, magnesium, and calcium.

items.headline: How obesity increases the risk of spine disorders and chronic back pain
items.gist: Back pain has become one of the most common health problems even as obesity has emerged as one of the fastest-growing public health challenges, yet fewer people realize that excess body weight places tremendous stress on the spine—patients in their thirties and forties are increasingly seen with accelerated spinal wear from weight rather than age alone. Every additional kilogram increases mechanical load on vertebrae, intervertebral discs, facet joints, and supporting muscles, accelerating degeneration and contributing to chronic pain; obesity is a modifiable risk factor linked to chronic low back pain, slipped disc (disc herniation), lumbar canal stenosis, facet joint arthritis, and degenerative disc disease.
items.paragraph: Back pain has become one of the most common health problems even as obesity has emerged as one of the fastest-growing public health challenges, yet fewer people realize that excess body weight places tremendous stress on the spine—patients in their thirties and forties are increasingly seen with accelerated spinal wear from weight rather than age alone. Every additional kilogram increases mechanical load on vertebrae, intervertebral discs, facet joints, and supporting muscles, accelerating degeneration and contributing to chronic pain; obesity is a modifiable risk factor linked to chronic low back pain, slipped disc (disc herniation), lumbar canal stenosis, facet joint arthritis, and degenerative disc disease. Weight loss can reduce mechanical stress, improve walking ability, decrease inflammation, and improve outcomes after spine surgery, though severely compressed nerves or advanced cord compression may still need medication, injections, or surgery; management also includes physiotherapy, core strengthening, healthy nutrition, and prevention through maintaining a healthy weight throughout adulthood.

items.headline: Brighten your smile naturally with activated charcoal
items.gist: Activated charcoal powder is derived from carbonaceous sources such as coconut husk, peat, wood, coir, nutshells, lignite, coal, and petroleum pitch through chemical or physical activation, yielding a fine, black, tasteless, odorless powder available at medical stores and pharmacies, typically in tablet form. It works as a teeth whitener by binding to rough tooth surfaces where stains, plaques, and yellow discoloration accumulate, using its large pores and adhesive properties to remove plaque, food particles, and surface stains; continuous use can noticeably improve tooth color.
items.paragraph: Activated charcoal powder is derived from carbonaceous sources such as coconut husk, peat, wood, coir, nutshells, lignite, coal, and petroleum pitch through chemical or physical activation, yielding a fine, black, tasteless, odorless powder available at medical stores and pharmacies, typically in tablet form. It works as a teeth whitener by binding to rough tooth surfaces where stains, plaques, and yellow discoloration accumulate, using its large pores and adhesive properties to remove plaque, food particles, and surface stains; continuous use can noticeably improve tooth color. Users grind one tablet into powder, mix with a few drops of water to form a paste, brush gently, and rinse thoroughly—though the article notes it is not suitable for decayed or cavity-stricken teeth.

items.headline: A colonial gaze: how the British imagined Bastar and its people
items.gist: An excerpt from Shantanu Nandan Sharma's Rebel Bastar describes how colonial accounts portrayed Bastar as a primitive woodland of cannibals — including Henry Harpur Spry's claim that its people 'sacrifice and eat their fellow creatures' without ever visiting — while flawed censuses produced wildly unreliable figures: the 1866 headcount recorded 2,69,684 people but the 1872 census showed an inexplicable 70% drop to 78,856, with J.W. Neill noting children were not enumerated in many villages and enumerators recorded colourful but inaccurate professions such as 'con man', 'pimp', and 'idiot'.

items.headline: China's laser mosquito killer
items.gist: A Chinese-developed device that uses lasers to detect and eliminate mosquitoes has moved into mass production, with the first units set to reach buyers before the end of August, developer Photon Matrix Lab said in an update on crowdfunding platform Indiegogo. The portable unit from Changzhou-based Photon Matrix Lab combines LiDAR, millimeter-wave radar and AI-powered computer vision to spot mosquitoes and similarly sized flying insects, then fires a precision laser to eliminate them mid-air; production began this month and an official online store is selling infrared and blue-laser versions directly to consumers.
items.paragraph: A Chinese-developed device that uses lasers to detect and eliminate mosquitoes has moved into mass production, with the first units set to reach buyers before the end of August, developer Photon Matrix Lab said in an update on crowdfunding platform Indiegogo. Similar systems exist outside China — Israeli company Bzigo's Iris ($299) locates mosquitoes with computer vision and infrared sensors but leaves elimination to the user — while Photon Matrix's claimed performance figures have not yet been independently verified and broader adoption will likely hinge on proven effectiveness, safety, reliability and price.

items.headline: 'Discipline' trade-off
items.gist: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu argues on X that leaning too hard on "discipline" can quietly kill the initiative organisations need, contrasting firms where employees look upward for direction against those where they act on their own judgment and push back on each other. He says organisations heavy on metrics tend toward the first model — predictable but only as good as leadership's calls — while initiative-led teams feel messier, argue more, and often rely on the market rather than internal process to impose order; attempting both a "disciplined culture of seizing the initiative" tends to backfire.

The post comes as Zoho contends with memory prices up roughly 500% over the past year, partly fuelled by AI data-centre demand, alongside rising AI token costs; Vembu says the firm has so far avoided passing costs to customers but maintaining that is growing tougher, and argues software development must shift toward leaner code as the assumption of cheap memory no longer holds.
