items.headline: SC quashes Rs 425-cr penalty over AI-generated precedents
items.gist: The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside a Rs 425.27-crore customs penalty imposed on diamond trader Vijay Ghanshyam Gadiya after finding that the adjudicating authority had relied on non-existent or incorrectly cited judicial precedents that appeared to have been generated or hallucinated by artificial intelligence. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu allowed the civil appeal and quashed both the Gujarat High Court order and the original customs adjudication order, which had been imposed by the Additional Commissioner of Customs, Surat, on the allegation that Gadiya had mis-declared a consignment of natural diamonds as lab-grown diamonds.
items.paragraph: The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside a Rs 425.27-crore customs penalty imposed on diamond trader Vijay Ghanshyam Gadiya after finding that the adjudicating authority had relied on non-existent or incorrectly cited judicial precedents that appeared to have been generated or hallucinated by artificial intelligence. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu allowed the civil appeal and quashed both the Gujarat High Court order and the original customs adjudication order, which had been imposed by the Additional Commissioner of Customs, Surat, on the allegation that Gadiya had mis-declared a consignment of natural diamonds as lab-grown diamonds. The court said decisions relying on fake or hallucinated material as precedent are invalid and that courts must adopt a zero-tolerance policy toward producing, citing, or using AI-generated precedents without verification.

items.headline: Juvenile held for creating fake Facebook account in IPS officer's name, duping people
items.gist: A juvenile from Rajasthan was apprehended for allegedly creating a fake Facebook account in the name of IPS officer Narayana M, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Electronic City Division) in Bengaluru, and collecting money from people on various pretexts; police recovered ₹2 lakh in cash allegedly obtained through fake bank accounts. A case was registered at Hebbagodi police station after the accused used the officer's photograph to send friend requests and demand money; investigation busted an organised network operating from Kota Khurd village in Rajasthan, with the juvenile revealing associates had created fake accounts in the names of several IAS and IPS officers across the country.

items.headline: Would AI disaster force humanity to act?
items.gist: Experts in Silicon Valley think that within the next couple of years there will be an extraordinary takeoff for artificial intelligence, described as "recursive self-improvement" — the point at which AI itself trains each successive model, resulting in exponential development of something that in many significant respects is more intelligent than humans. Elon Musk predicts "an age of amazing abundance" but also sees a 10–20% chance of killer robots murdering us all, while Geoffrey Hinton, one of the intellectual founding fathers of AI, told an interviewer in 2023: "My intuition is, we're toast." As Robert Wright puts it in his book The God Test, the near-term future holds a wide array of not-implausible paths for humankind that would be wildly transformative — but whether that means heaven or hell remains sharply contested.

items.headline: Hyundai India MD seeks long-term policy
items.gist: Hyundai Motor India MD and CEO Tarun Garg on Wednesday called for a consistent long-term policy framework to support scale and accelerate technology and component development, while urging the country's auto industry to move beyond exporting conventional components to advanced technologies, engineering capabilities and innovation. items.headline: Rising sea levels, millions at risk, but are we ready?
items.gist: A UN report warns millions in cities such as Kolkata and Mumbai face immediate risk of losing homes to rising sea levels and permanent inundation, with NASA and IPCC projections putting roughly 12 Indian coastal cities and towns at risk of submersion by up to 2.7 to 3 feet; Chennai, Kochi, Visakhapatnam and Mangaluru are among those facing accelerated rise, cyclone intensity or imminent danger. By 2040, more than 10% of land in Mumbai, Yanam and Thoothukudi could submerge, while India’s adaptation efforts include ₹1,000 crore for resettling displaced coastal populations and ₹1,500 crore for erosion mitigation under the 15th Finance Commission, though the article notes policy remains diffused and insufficiently integrated on the ground.

items.headline: Should AI be taxed?
items.gist: Warnings that AI will take jobs have intensified as thousands of employees worldwide receive layoff emails on a near-monthly basis — what Indian economist Raghuram Rajan has called a "jobocalypse." Rajan, former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India and a member of the US Federal Reserve policy review panel, has suggested levying a tax on corporate firms' use of artificial intelligence to help governments continue earning tax revenues that nations would have received from a human workforce. In an August 2026 column titled "How Corporations Can Mitigate an AI Jobocalypse," he wrote that AI-related job displacement is coming, though no one knows how fast it will proceed, how far it will go, or which sectors it will affect most.

items.headline: AI eats traffic, websites block AI, making reliable information scarce
items.gist: For 30 years the world wide web has run on a social contract in which most sites are free for search engines to access but users who draw on their content give credit by linking to the source — a contract now collapsing as AI tools crawl sites not to link to them but to train models and generate answers. Cloudflare, which manages 30% or more of the top 10,000 internet sites, estimates over half of all web traffic is now AI bots; as websites lose traffic and revenue, many are blocking AI scrapers, meaning AI results depend more on low-quality websites, including many generated by AI.
items.paragraph: For 30 years the world wide web has run on a social contract in which most sites are free for search engines to access but users who draw on their content give credit by linking to the source — a contract now collapsing as AI tools crawl sites not to link to them but to train models and generate answers. Cloudflare, which manages 30% or more of the top 10,000 internet sites, estimates over half of all web traffic is now AI bots; as websites lose traffic and revenue, many are blocking AI scrapers, meaning AI results depend more on low-quality websites, including many generated by AI. From September 15, Cloudflare sites will block AI crawlers by default on pages containing advertising — potentially removing up to 30% of the world's top sites from Google AI Overviews summaries — while studies already show around one in six sources used by AI search tools is itself an AI-generated website, raising the risk of model collapse as AI models train on more AI text.

items.headline: ChatGPT drops custom stickers for mobile users
items.gist: OpenAI has rolled out a feature called Stickers in ChatGPT, allowing users to generate personalised sticker packs directly from text prompts and share them in everyday conversations; it went live globally for mobile ChatGPT users, according to an OpenAI announcement. Users can remix stickers with emojis and pick from as many as 18 visual styles — including Holographic, Anime and 3D — and the feature is free and available to all mobile ChatGPT users worldwide, though OpenAI has not specified whether it will extend to desktop or web versions.

items.headline: Migration and Kerala's choices (Opinion)
items.gist: Kerala policymakers seeking to reverse emigration must ask whether the state's labour and academic markets can absorb migrants, argue Sonal Kuruvilla and Fahad Hasin, noting that people leave when second-best local options pay too little and that building thick urban labour markets with minimal regulatory friction is the real policy challenge rather than stopping departures.

items.headline: Statistical illusion (Opinion)

items.headline: Prices keep spiralling (Opinion)
items.gist: Steep hikes in jet fuel and commercial LPG prices add to the pain of Indian travellers and consumers, with commercial LPG up by ₹10 likely cascading into food and industrial production costs. The writer argues that 7.8% GDP growth means little if government policy does not relieve common people’s economic woes, and only a pro-people, pro-poor government can ensure justice for all sections.

items.headline: A cesspit of shame (Opinion)

items.headline: 'Early Harvest' — larger but not necessarily safer (Opinion)
items.gist: At August 25, 2026 special representative talks in Beijing, an August 26 "Eight Points" document restored "Early and Substantial Harvest" for boundary delimitation and border management—India's coinage from around 2019 as a counter to China's Sikkim-only proposal. A genuine Early Harvest requires highest-watershed delineation, trijunction points excluded per the 2012 Common Understanding, and terms of reference extending India's 2019 proposal.

items.headline: Manusmriti is counter to equality. That’s why BJP-RSS is rattled (Opinion)
items.gist: After Rahul Gandhi urged women in Pune on 22 August to “smash the patriarchy” and reject the “Manusmriti mindset,” and condemned a ‘purification’ ritual in Haldwani following Dalit Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s speech, BJP-RSS leaders defended the ceremony and an FIR was filed against Gandhi. items.headline: Unconditional dependence (Opinion)
items.gist: Swami Sivayoganandhaji writes that bhakti yoga suits the Kali Yuga, citing Lord Krishna's teaching that a devotee whose mind is fixed on Him every moment with complete faith and unconditional dependence is the best exponent of yoga. items.headline: Constitutional faultlines in FCRA Bill (Opinion)
items.gist: Thajaswini C.B. and Siddharth Dev Prasad argue the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 goes beyond regulating foreign contributions by creating a statutory 'Designated Authority' to oversee the vesting, supervision, management, and disposal of foreign contributions and assets when an organisation's FCRA certificate is cancelled, surrendered, or ceases to exist — potentially extending to management of the organisation's activities — raising constitutional questions about executive overreach, proportionality, and whether safeguards for restoration, revision, and appeal are sufficiently clear and timely.
